 THREE
STRAND/THEME/TOPIC: CHRISTIAN VALUES
SUBSTRAND/SUB-THEME/SUB-TOPIC: Honesty (Ananias and Sapphira)
Specific lesson learning outcome.
By the end of the lesson, the learner should be to narrate the story of Ananias and Sapphira and desire to be honest in
their lives.
KEY INQUIRY QUESTION (s)
How do we celebrate Easter? Which activities take place during Easter?
 Core competencies Values PCIs
 Imagination and  Honesty Decision making
 creativity  Trust Self-esteem
  Learning to learn  Responsibility
  Communication and  Sharing
 collaboration
LEARNING RESOURCES
Good news bible.
Props and costumes for the role play.
Learner’s Book 3 page 66-68.
ORGANIZATION OF LEARNING
Learners to work in pairs or groups.
INTRODUCTION
Review the previous lesson.
LESSON DEVELOPMENT (Assessment as learning)
 Step 1: Direct learners to the picture on page 66 of the learner’s book.
 Step 2: Direct learners to activity 1 and lead them through the questions.
 Step 3: Select some learners and help them to find and read the story from the bible.
 Step 4: Ask learners why it is good to tell the truth always and guide learners into appreciation that telling the truth
 is good.
 Step 5: Direct the learners through activity 2
SUMMARY
Learners to read summary notes.
CONCLUSION (Assessment of Learning)
Learners to ask and answer question and inform them of the next lesson.
EXTENSION OF ACTIVITIES
Encourage learners to practice honesty at home.

SUBSTRAND/SUB-THEME/SUB-TOPIC: Giving offering in church
Specific lesson learning outcome.
By the end of the lesson, the learner should be to practice honesty by taking offerings to church.
KEY INQUIRY QUESTION (s)
Why should you be honest with church offering?
 Core competencies Values PCIs
  Self-efficacy  Honesty Decision making
  Communication and  Trust Self-esteem
 collaboration  Responsibility assertiveness
  Sharing
LEARNING RESOURCES
Good news bible.
Flash cars with short descriptions of situations where the learners have to choose between being honest or disobedient or
dishonest with their church offerings.
Learner’s Book 3 page 68-69.
ORGANIZATION OF LEARNING
Learners to work in pairs or groups.
INTRODUCTION
Review the previous lesson.
LESSON DEVELOPMENT (Assessment as learning)
 Step 1: Remind the learners of the illustration of Jane giving offering in church on page 66 and ask learners to
 activity 3 .
 Step 2: Select some learners and help them to find and read the story from the bible.
 Step 3: Guide learners to the understanding that the story of Ananias and Sapphira teaches us to be honest in giving
 offerings in church.
 Step 4: Lead the learners to commit to being honest with their offerings in church and learners to copy the notes in
 their books.
SUMMARY
Learners to read summary notes.
CONCLUSION (Assessment of Learning)
Learners to ask and answer question and inform them of the next lesson.
EXTENSION OF ACTIVITIES
Encourage learners to practice honesty at home.

STRAND/THEME/TOPIC: CHRISTIAN VALUES
SUBSTRAND/SUB-THEME/SUB-TOPIC: Respecting other people’s items
Specific lesson learning outcome.
By the end of the lesson, the learner should be to explain the importance of respecting other people’s items for
harmonious living.
KEY INQUIRY QUESTION (s)
What do you do when you find lost items?
 Core competencies Values PCIs
  Self-efficacy  Honesty Decision making
  Communication and  Respect Self-esteem
 collaboration  Responsibility assertiveness
  Imagination and
 creativity
LEARNING RESOURCES
Good news bible.
Flash cars with situations requiring respect for other people’s items.
Learner’s tablets.
Learner’s Book 3 page 70-71.
ORGANIZATION OF LEARNING
Learners to work in pairs or groups
INTRODUCTION
Review the previous lesson
LESSON DEVELOPMENT (Assessment as learning)
 Step 1: Direct the attention of the learners to the key inquiry question and ask them to carry out activity 5.
 Step 2: Using questions, remind learners of the story Ananias and Sapphira
 Step 3: Guide learners to know that taking and keeping a lost item is cheating.
 Step 4: Guide learners to commit to not keeping for themselves lost items that they may come across and direct them
 to activity 6.
SUMMARY
Learners to read summary notes.
CONCLUSION (Assessment of Learning)
Learners to ask and answer question and inform them of the next lesson.
EXTENSION OF ACTIVITIES
Encourage learners to practice honesty at home.

 THREE

SUBSTRAND/SUB-THEME/SUB-TOPIC: Respecting other people’s items
Specific lesson learning outcome.
By the end of the lesson, the learner should be to explain the importance of respecting other people’s items for
harmonious living.
KEY INQUIRY QUESTION (s)
What do you do when you find lost items?
 Core competencies Values PCIs
  Self-efficacy  Honesty Decision making
  Communication and  Respect Self-esteem
 collaboration  Responsibility assertiveness
  Imagination and
 creativity
LEARNING RESOURCES
Good news bible.
Flash cars with situations requiring respect for other people’s items.
Learner’s tablets.
Learner’s Book 3 page 70-71.
ORGANIZATION OF LEARNING
Learners to work in pairs or groups.
INTRODUCTION
Review the previous lesson.
LESSON DEVELOPMENT (Assessment as learning)
 Step 1: Ask learners how they feel if someone took their items or used them without first asking for permission.
 Step 2: Using questions, remind learners of what happened to Ananias and Sapphira after they died.
 Step 3: Lead learners to appreciate that when they take other people’s items or use them without permission they are
 not honest or respectful.
 Step 4: Guide learners to commit to never taking or using other people’s items without their permission.
 Step 5: Present some situations to the learners and ask them to state what would be the honest thing to do in those
 situations.
SUMMARY
Learners to read summary notes.
CONCLUSION (Assessment of Learning)
Learners to ask and answer question and inform them of the next lesson.
EXTENSION OF ACTIVITIES
Encourage learners to practice honesty at home.

STRAND/THEME/TOPIC: CHRISTIAN VALUES
SUBSTRAND/SUB-THEME/SUB-TOPIC: Thankfulness
Specific lesson learning outcome.
By the end of the lesson, the learner should be to describe ways if thanking God for creating them.
KEY INQUIRY QUESTION (s)
How can I thank God for creating me?
 Core competencies Values PCIs
  Self-efficacy  Thankfulness Decision making
  Communication and  Humility Self-esteem
 collaboration  Trust Self-awareness
  Imagination and  Responsibility
 creativity
  Learning to learn
LEARNING RESOURCES
Good news bible.
Chart showing ways in which to thank God for creating us.
Manila paper, crayons.
Learner’s tablets.
Learner’s Book 3 page 72-73.
ORGANIZATION OF LEARNING
Learners to work in pairs or groups.
INTRODUCTION
Review the previous lesson.
LESSON DEVELOPMENT (Assessment as learning)
 Step 1: Call the attention of the learners the Key inquiry questions and direct them to undertake Activity 1.
 Step 2: Select some learners to read out loud the Bible verse.
 Step 3: Lead learners to appreciate that the bible tells them to thank God for His love
 Step 4: Guide learners to appreciate the love that God has shown them by creating them and therefore commit to
 thanking Him.
 Step 5: Put up the chart and work with the learners to identify ways in which they can thank God for creating them.
SUMMARY
Learners to read summary notes.
CONCLUSION (Assessment of Learning)
Learners to ask and answer question and inform them of the next lesson.
EXTENSION OF ACTIVITIES
Encourage learners to make “thank you” cards.

SUBSTRAND/SUB-THEME/SUB-TOPIC: Thanking God for other people
Specific lesson learning outcome.
By the end of the lesson, the learner should be to thank God for their family, friends and teachers, and appreciate them
all the time.
KEY INQUIRY QUESTION (s)
Why should I thank God for other people?
 Core competencies Values PCIs
  Self-efficacy  Thankfulness Decision making
  Communication and  Humility Self-esteem
 collaboration  Trust Self-awareness
  Imagination and  Responsibility
 creativity

Good news bible.
Flash cards showing reasons for thanking God for other people.
Manila paper, crayons.
Learner’s tablets.
Learner’s Book 3 page 74-75.
ORGANIZATION OF LEARNING
Learners to work in pairs or groups.
INTRODUCTION
Review the previous lesson.
LESSON DEVELOPMENT (Assessment as learning)
 Step 1: Ask learners whether they thank God for their families, friends and teachers and direct them to activity 3.
 Step 2: Remind learners of Psalms 136:1.
 Step 3: Guide learners to understand that these other people in their lives are a show of God’s love for them.
 Step 4: Lead learners to identify the various ways in which they can thank God for the people in their lives and
 direct them to activity 4.
SUMMARY
Learners to read summary notes.
CONCLUSION (Assessment of Learning)
Learners to ask and answer question and inform them of the next lesson.

 THREE
STRAND/THEME/TOPIC: CHRISTIAN VALUES
SUBSTRAND/SUB-THEME/SUB-TOPIC: Forgiveness (the story of the unforgiving servant)
Specific lesson learning outcome.
By the end of the lesson, the learner should be to describe the story of the unforgiving servant and relate it to their
interaction with others.
KEY INQUIRY QUESTION (s)
What did the unforgiving servant do? What do we learn from the story of the unforgiving servant?
 Core competencies Values PCIs
  Learning to learn  Forgiveness Decision making
  Communication and  Love Self-esteem
 collaboration  Humility Self-awareness
  Imagination and  Tolerance
 creativity  Kindness, social justice
  Citizenship
LEARNING RESOURCES
Good news bible.
Props and costumes for role play.
Learner’s tablets.
Learner’s Book 3 page 74-75.
ORGANIZATION OF LEARNING
Learners to work in pairs or groups
INTRODUCTION
Review the previous lesson.
LESSON DEVELOPMENT (Assessment as learning)
 Step 1: Direct learners attention to the key inquiry questions and to tackle part one of activity 1
 Step 2: Guide learners to undertake part two of activity 1.
 Step 3: Select some learners to read the story out aloud from the bible.
 Step 4: Guide the learners to see the wrong in how the unforgiving servant was forgiven but refused to forgive his
 fellow servant and lead learners to equate the story to God and themselves.
 Step 5: Direct learners to question 1 of Activity 2.
SUMMARY
Learners to read summary notes.
CONCLUSION (Assessment of Learning)
Learners to ask and answer question and inform them of the next lesson.
EXTENSION OF ACTIVITIES
Encourage learners to observe within the school what happens when people do not forgive each other.

Specific lesson learning outcome.
By the end of the lesson, the learner should be to:
 1. Identify people they can trust for their own safety.
 2. Mention the people to report to incase of danger for appropriate action to be taken.
KEY INQUIRY QUESTION (s)
Who are the people you trust?
 Core competencies Values PCIs
  Learning to learn  Trust Decision making
  Communication and  Integrity Self-esteem
 collaboration  Responsibility Self-awareness
  Self-efficacy assertiveness
  Critical thinking
LEARNING RESOURCES
Good news bible.
Learner’s Book 3 page 80-81.
ORGANIZATION OF LEARNING
Learners to work in pairs or groups.
INTRODUCTION
Review the previous lesson.
LESSON DEVELOPMENT (Assessment as learning)
 Step 1: Use questions to direct the learners to the meaning of the word “trust”. Draw the attention of the learners to
 the key inquiry question.
 Step 2: Direct learners to activity 1. Let them look at the pictures then attempt to answer questions that follow.
 Step 3: Lead learners in identifying other people they can trust and report to when they are in danger.
SUMMARY
Learners to read summary notes.
CONCLUSION (Assessment of Learning)
Learners to ask and answer question and inform them of the next lesson.
EXTENSION OF ACTIVITIES
Encourage learners to practice what to do in case they are in danger.

STRAND/THEME/TOPIC: CHRISTIAN VALUES
SUBSTRAND/SUB-THEME/SUB-TOPIC: Talking about others
Specific lesson learning outcome.
By the end of the lesson, the learner should be to discuss the effects of talking about others for harmonious living.
KEY INQUIRY QUESTION (s)
Why is it wrong to talk about others?
 Core competencies Values PCIs
  Learning to learn  Trust Decision making
  Communication and  Integrity Empathy
 collaboration  Responsibility Self-awareness
  Self-efficacy  Love Friendship formation
  Critical thinking  Respect
LEARNING RESOURCES
Good news bible.
Learner’s Book 3 page 82-83.
ORGANIZATION OF LEARNING
Learners to work in pairs or groups.
INTRODUCTION
Review the previous lesson.
LESSON DEVELOPMENT (Assessment as learning)
 Step 1: Bring to the attention of the learners the key inquiry questions.
 Step 2: Direct learners to activity 3. Let them look at the picture and answer the questions.
 Step 3: inform the learners that the Bible guides us on talking about others.
 Step 4: Select some learners to take turns reading the verse from the Bible.
 Step 5: Guide the learners to talk about what they think the bible verse means. Lead learners to appreciate that
 gossiping causes hurt and conflict.
 Step 6: Ask them what they will do when someone wants them to gossip, and lead them state and demonstrate that
 they will refuse. Direct learners to activity 4.
SUMMARY
Learners to read summary notes.
CONCLUSION (Assessment of Learning)
Learners to ask and answer question and inform them of the next lesson.
EXTENSION OF ACTIVITIES
Encourage learners to practice what to do in case they are in danger.

ORGANIZATION OF LEARNING

INTRODUCTION.
Review the previous lesson.
LESSON DEVELOPMENT (Assessment as learning)
 Step 1: Have learners stand up from their desks and sing and dance to the song.
 Step 2: Direct learners attention to the song under activity 5.
 Step 3: Have some learners read Proverbs 11:13.
 Step 4: Guide learners to appreciate that gossiping destroys trust; they cannot be trusted if they gossip.
 Step 5: Have the learners agree to always put themselves in the other person’s position before they gossip.
 Step 6: Pose the question you prepared earlier to the learners to gauge how well they have acquired knowledge on
 the value of trust.
SUMMARY
Learners to read summary notes.
CONCLUSION (Assessment of Learning)
Learners to ask and answer question and inform them of the next lesson.
EXTENSION OF ACTIVITIES
Encourage learners to practice what to do in case they are in danger.
